issue_context.title: Remove deprecated methods in 4.0.0
issue_context.body:
<!--
Feature Requests:
  Please read https://github.com/jquery/jquery/wiki/Adding-new-features
  Most features should start as plugins outside of jQuery.

Bug Reports:
  Note that we only can fix bugs in the latest version of jQuery.
  Briefly describe the issue you've encountered
  *  What do you expect to happen?
  *  What actually happens?
  *  Which browsers are affected?
  Provide a *minimal* test case, see https://webkit.org/test-case-reduction/
  Use the latest shipping version of jQuery in your test case!
  We prefer test cases on https://jsbin.com or https://jsfiddle.net

Frequently Reported Issues:
  * Selectors with '#' break: See https://github.com/jquery/jquery/issues/2824
-->

### Description ###
We've deprecated some methods in 3.x (like `jQuery.camelCase`), we should remember to remove them all in 4.0. Looking at `deprecated.js` should be a good start; other APIs to remove:
- [x] `jQuery.cssProps`.
- [x] `jQuery.cssNumber` (removed in #4055).

### Link to test case ###
comments: @mgol I want to submit a PR for this.. Is this issue still relevant?

@ShashankaNataraj It is, though we're not working on jQuery 4.0 yet. You can submit a PR, though. You'd need to look at each of the deprecated APIs; some are in `deprecated.js`, some are only deprecated in docs: [3.0](https://api.jquery.com/category/deprecated/deprecated-3.0/) & [3.3](https://api.jquery.com/category/deprecated/deprecated-3.3/) and some may only have an API issue created but the deprecations are not documented yet: https://github.com/jquery/api.jquery.com/issues?utf8=%E2%9C%93&q=is%3Aissue+is%3Aopen+deprecate.

For ones that have API docs tickets, we should first document the deprecation before we remove it on `master`; we're a little understaffed when it comes to content sites (like api.jquery.com) so especially there help would be appreciated. Thanks!

review_comments:
This does make the test a little less isolated but it's already been that way since `finalPropName` has been refactored by @dmethvin to use an internal `vendorProps` map so we're not losing much here.

Another test can influence this one if it sets some transform- or appearance-related props. We can think if there's any way around that but, as I said, it's already an issue.
